author: TEDx Talks
description:
Genetic ancestry testing promises answers about who you are and where you come from — but what happens when the results turn your world upside down? In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Professor Emma Kowal from Deakin University, Melbourne, Australia, explores how at-home DNA tests are reshaping ideas of family, kinship, and personal identity.

This talk explores how DNA testing and genetic ancestry tests can uncover surprising family connections, the social and emotional impact of genetic discoveries, and how ancestry testing challenges traditional ideas of kinship, heritage, and identity. It also encourages viewers to reflect on the questions to ask before taking an at-home DNA test.

Watch now to rethink what really makes a family and explore the hidden power of your genetic story.
Professor Emma Kowal is an anthropologist whose work examines the intersections of science, medicine, and Indigenous studies. A former medical doctor and public health researcher, she is Professor of An
title: The DNA test that could change everything | Emma Kowal | TEDxDeakin Uni Melbourne

author: TEDx Talks
description: Robert Puchalla explores why so many change initiatives fail, and why fear is often the silent force holding people back. Through personal moments of crisis, surprising stories, and insights from his work with organizations, he reveals how “change-washing” creates disengagement and resignation. Robert introduces three powerful questions that help individuals rethink their choices, build courage, and transform uncertainty into opportunity. His talk inspires leaders and employees alike to take responsibility, embrace authenticity, and create cultures where real change can thrive. A compelling call to stop fearing change and start using it to shape a better future. Robert Puchalla is a Managing Director, culture designer and lecturer who unites strategy with emotional intelligence. With a background in brand leadership, marketing and organizational change, he empowers people and companies to replace “changewashing” with real mindset shifts and so to enable them to gain a higher performan
title: Stop changewashing - start mindsetting | Robert Puchalla | TEDxNuremberg

author: TEDx Talks
description: Guenes shows how cultural diversity becomes a true superpower — not by itself, but through belonging, empathy, and connection. Drawing on his multicultural background and international business experience, he shares personal stories and insights that reveal how small acts of kindness and bridge-building turn differences into strength for teams, communities, and society. Guenes Guenaydin is a digital sales leader with a multicultural background and a strong belief in the power of human connection. Raised by a Turkish family in Germany and having lived in Türkiye, Austria, Germany, the U.S., and Ireland, he brings a deeply international perspective to his work. Today, he leads a Digital Sales team, helping organizations rethink customer experience and the future of work. His passion for belonging and cultural diversity is rooted in his migration story and strengthened through years of personal & business experiences. His mission is to show how empathy turns diversity into a superpower.
title: Has cultural diversity really failed? | Guenes Guenaydin | TEDxNuremberg

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Milena invites us to rethink what it means to be responsible in a world shaped by conflict. Drawing from her doctoral research and her experiences across regions such as Mexico, Uganda, and Vietnam, she explores what happens when ethics meets reality — when companies operate in places where peace and justice can’t be taken for granted. Milena challenges the illusion of corporate neutrality and exposes how silence, whether chosen or imposed, can make businesses complicit in harm.

Blending insights from historical thinkers with real-world examples, she calls for a reimagining of business as a moral actor — one capable of thought, reflection, and compassion even amid conflict. Her talk is both a warning and a call to courage: to break the silence, reclaim responsibility, and let ethical thought become ethical action.  Milena Störmer is a doctoral researcher at Friedrich-Alexander University Erlangen-Nürnberg, where she studies how businesses operate in environments where peace, justice,
title: The silence of business in war | Milena Störmer | TEDxNuremberg

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if organizations weren’t just places we work, but living social systems that shape who we become?
In her TEDx Talk, Arina pulls back the curtain on the psychology behind teams, relationships, and human courage. With bold insights and years of leadership experience, she reveals the three keys that help people grow, connect, and perform at their highest level. Her message is clear: when we use these three keys, we unlock human potential within organizations in ways we never thought possible. This talk will change the way you see work, leadership ... and maybe even yourself. Arina Zonner is a business psychologist (M.Sc.) and business lawyer (LL.B.), a certified Scrum Master, and an experienced senior leader in management. She is a recognized expert in HR, organizational culture, and leadership. In addition to her executive background, Arina is a published author, keynote speaker, and content creator specializing in organizational development, strategy, work psychology, and change m
title: 3 keys to redesign organizational mindset | Arina Zonner | TEDxNuremberg

author: TEDx Talks
description: Behavioral addictions are widespread, deeply stigmatized, and often poorly treated. Etienne Atangana, a senior neuroscience student researcher at the University of Miami, has seen this firsthand through his personal experience with behavioral addiction and navigating the mental health care system. In this talk, Etienne challenges the way psychiatric treatment is currently practiced, arguing that while other areas of medicine have embraced precision and biology, mental health care still relies largely on subjective self-reported data. He introduces computational psychiatry, an emerging field that combines math, neuroscience, and data science, as a path toward more personalized and effective treatment. This talk aims to transform the audience’s view on how we should treat mental illness, and what it would look like to bring true precision to mental health care. Etienne Atangana is a senior neuroscience major at the University of Miami. He has conducted neuroscience research at prestigio
title: Computational psychiatry and the future of mental health care | Etienne Atangana | TEDxUMiami

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, Adriana de Moura, international art dealer and reality TV argues that in a world obsessed with comparison and curated perfection, authenticity is not just self-expression, but a strategic and transformative advantage. She illustrates this through her personal journey of abandoning her creative identity for a "safe" legal career, only to find profound despair. Her pivotal moment came when she rejected comparison and chose self-acceptance, leading her to open an art gallery. This one authentic decision unlocked her unique strengths, leading to unexpected success in television and music. Adriana de Moura is best known as the “Brazilian bombshell” on the Bravo’s hit television show— The Real Housewives of Miami. However, Adriana’s true passion is her career as an art dealer. From a very tender age, Adriana was introduced to art by her grandmother who was a painter. After being influenced by her grandmother’s artwork, the Brazilian native pursued her education to study abroad
title: The impact of authenticity in a culture of comparison | Adriana de Moura | TEDxUMiami

author: TEDx Talks
description: Nicole Lopez-Alvar shares how growing up with her twin brother AJ, who has autism and epilepsy, reshaped the way she sees the world. While AJ’s life doesn’t follow traditional milestones, his presence taught her that different does not mean less. Through him, she learned to listen to overlooked voices, redefine impact beyond achievement, and pursue storytelling rooted in empathy. This talk invites us to expand our understanding of love, inclusion, and what truly makes a life meaningful. Nicole Lopez-Alvar is a Miami-born journalist and cultural storyteller known for spotlighting the people, restaurants, and communities shaping South Florida. She is the Food Editor at Miami New Times, where she covers dining, chefs, and the city’s evolving food identity. Prior to that role, she worked as a digital journalist with WPLG Local 10 News and WSVN 7 News, reporting on breaking news and culture across the region. A University of Miami School of Communication alumna, Nicole brings a sharp edito
title: My Twin, My Teacher | Nicole Lopez-Alvar | TEDxUMiami

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Olga Lykova knows what it feels like to have no backup plan. In this powerful and deeply personal talk, she takes us on a journey from immigrating to the United States with $5,000, to losing everything in a robbery at age twelve, to facing career rejection and even surviving a house fire while six months pregnant. Through fear, uncertainty, and moments where freezing would have been easier, Olga shares the one question that changed her life and career: What can I build now? This talk invites us to rethink resilience, decision-making, and why some of the most defining moments in our lives don’t come with a Plan B. Olga Lykova is a partnerships executive, keynote speaker, and podcast host known for helping businesses scale through strategic partner ecosystems. She serves as Head of Partnerships, North America at monday.com, where she leads growth and go-to-market strategy through alliances. 

Over the last decade, Olga has built and managed global partner teams that contributed 50–80% o
title: How to thrive when there is no plan B | Olga Lykova | TEDxUMiami

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In a world filled with visibility, we often assume the greatest threat comes from being watched. But what happens when the gaze no longer comes from outside, when we carry it within ourselves?
In this talk, Messiah explores how surveillance quietly shifted from something imposed upon us to something we perform for ourselves and one another.
Drawing on cultural examples, social theory, and personal reflection, he traces how social performance moved from being situational to ambient - shaping how we speak, relate, fail, and even try.
He invites the audience to consider what is lost when performance never ends, and what might become possible if we allowed ourselves to be visible before we were ready.
 Messiah Godfred Majid is a Stamps Scholar and international student from Accra, Ghana, studying Mathematics, Computer Science, and Biology at the University of Miami. His academic work focuses on the intersection of computational biology and biotechnology, particularly how emerging technolo
title: How we learned to watch ourselves | Messiah Godfried Majid | TEDxUMiami

author: TEDx Talks
description: Before we make a single conscious decision, our environment has already shaped our attention, our behavior, and our sense of self. In this talk, Naz Usman, a fifth-year architecture student at the University of Miami, explores how identity is not formed by discipline alone, but quietly constructed through the spaces we inhabit every day. Drawing from personal experience and a design project addressing stigma around the opioid epidemic in Lisbon, she reveals how environments can either suppress growth or make it feel almost inevitable. Rather than framing burnout and inconsistency as personal failure, the talk reframes them as environmental feedback, signals that something around us needs to change. Architecture, she argues, doesn’t just organize space; it organizes attention, safety, and possibility. When environments are designed with intention, growth becomes less about forcing change and more about removing the barriers that keep us stuck. We build our environments—and in turn, the
title: How Our Environments Shape Our Identity | Naz Usman | TEDxUMiami

author: TEDx Talks
description: Every day, people perfect their schedule to a science, doing the same things over and over and rarely changing anything. This rut means going from active participant to merely passive observer of your own life. In this talk, Timothy Sturtevant addresses why rigid routines are not only bad for your brain, but also worse for your soul. Sturtevant makes the case for adding more spontaneity into our lives and highlights ways that doing as little as one new thing per day can transform us. He provides actionable steps and encouragement to take steps on your own journey toward spontaneity. Timothy Sturtevant is a junior at Sam Houston State University in the Honors College, double majoring in Animation and Film/TV Production. When not pursuing the arts, Timothy is truly living spontaneously, whether it be learning how to juggle for no reason or practicing with the SHSU inline hockey team, for which he serves as head of logistics. While growing up as a military brat in Abilene, Texas, he lear
title: How spontaneity can transform your life | Timothy Sturtevant | TEDxSHSU

author: TEDx Talks
description: Opera, with its soaring melodies and dramatic narratives, has long captivated audiences, but beneath the spectacle lies a deeper mythic structure. In this talk, Dr. Rebecca Renfro explores how Joseph Campbell’s Hero’s Journey framework reveals the timeless psychological and spiritual arcs embedded in operatic storytelling. From Mozart’s The Magic Flute to Puccini’s Tosca, Renfro traces the path of transformation, trials, and transcendence that mirrors humanity’s deepest quests. By decoding these archetypes, she uncovers how opera doesn’t just entertain; it initiates, heals, and connects us to the universal myth within. Whether you’re a seasoned opera lover or a curious newcomer, this journey will change how you hear the music. Dr. Rebecca Renfro is a Professor of Music at Sam Houston State University, where she holds the titles of Director of Opera Workshop and Studio Voice Instructor. Directing credits include productions for Greater Worcester Opera, Opera del West, University of Con
title: Resurrecting the dead: Opera and the power of storytelling | Rebecca Renfro | TEDxSHSU

author: TEDx Talks
description: As digital technologies continue to transform how we work, learn, and communicate, this talk examines the growing importance of human-centered skills. Prof. Dana Alsulaiman explores people skills such as communication, empathy, and collaboration, and explains their role in supporting ethical innovation and effective leadership. Designed for students and educators alike, this talk emphasizes why technical expertise alone is not enough —and how human skills complement technology to create a meaningful and sustainable progress. Since joining JAUST three years ago, she established the BioMAD Lab, which focuses on developing biomaterials and next-generation technologies for minimally-invasive disease diagnosis and personalized healthcare, completed her undergraduate and master’s degrees in biomedical engineering at Imperial College London in 2015 and was then granted the prestigious President’s PhD Scholarship to support her doctoral studies. In 2019, she moved to the USA to pursue a postd
title: Are You Human Enough? | Dana Alsulaiman | TEDxAGS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: From the classroom to the court, we are constantly shaped by the people around us—teammates, classmates, coaches, and friends. In this talk, Malak Alassiri explores how everyday interactions in sports and school influence confidence, discipline, and decision-making. Drawing connections between teamwork on the court and growth in the classroom, she highlights how positive influence can push us to perform better, aim higher, and grow stronger—both as students and as individuals. This talk encourages young people to recognize the power of their environment and to become the kind of influence they want to see in others. . This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Between the Classroom and the Court | Malak Alassiri | TEDxAGS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk journalist Charmain Mukurazhizha unpacks the power of community and how healing and impact are rooted in presence rather than perfection. Through personal experiences of trauma silence and eventual healing the speaker shows how isolation deepens pain while community creates space for survival and growth. Drawing on African proverbs and lived experience the talk challenges the idea that strength means carrying everything alone and instead emphasizes the importance of showing up sitting in discomfort and choosing connection. The central message is simple yet urgent that checking in asking twice and refusing to look away matters because everyday acts of presence can save lives and remind people they were never meant to carry their pain alone. Charmaine Mukurazhizha is a Zimbabwean-born journalist, storyteller, and media creative passionate about elevating narratives at the intersection of culture, faith, women’s empowerment, food, and sports. Born and raised in Harare, she b
title: Bother them: Unpacking the power of community | Charmaine Mukurazhizha | TEDxUMiami

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this captivating TEDxTalk, Ron Jackson delves into the hidden power of memory, revealing how the stories we carry from our past quietly shape our choices, beliefs, and the way we love. He explains this phenomenon using a term he created -  “Message Imprints.” With warmth and wit, Jackson invites us to explore the invisible threads connecting our earliest experiences to our present relationships—whether they’re first dates, challenging partnerships, or lifelong marriages. By shining a light on the subconscious influence of memory and message imprints, he challenges us to question our assumptions, confront the echoes of old wounds, and discover the keys to building joyful, resilient connections. This talk is a call to reflection and action: to understand ourselves, to nurture healthier bonds, and ultimately, to create lives filled with greater happiness and meaning. Dr. Ronald L. Jackson II is Professor and Chair of the Department of Communication Studies at University of Miami, and
title: How memories quietly shape the present | Ronald L. Jackson II | TEDxUMiami

description:
The Day I Chose to Live is a TEDx talk about our darkest moments and how they can become doorways that lead us home to ourselves.
Thought Leader and Mentor Debbie Zita takes you into a defining day in her own life - one marked by profound desperation and an unflinching question about her reason for existing. With warmth and candor, she shares how that day became a turning point..
Through lived experience and grounded insight, Debbie offers practical ways to transform darkness into light, trauma into truth, and survival into a conscious choice to truly LIVE!

description: Why do some struggle to fall in love? Boran Cui explains how aphantasia might make falling in love harder, challenging the common belief that love is purely social. Initially inspired by a TikTok clip about aphantasia, he conducts research on the link between mental imagery and romantic responses, emphasizing that “Observation turns confusion into curiosity. Disruption turns belief into questioning. Reorganization turns questions into knowledge.” Student at the Affiliated High School of Peking University, psychology and neuroscience research rookie. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Quando pensamos no Brasil, imaginamos calor, festa, samba e cor. Mas existe um outro Brasil — silencioso, horizontal, feito de pampas infinitos, rodas de mate e histórias que passam de geração em geração.

Nesta fala, Luiza nos convida a conhecer o Brasil que raramente aparece nos cartões-postais: a cultura gaúcha, seus mitos, seus valores e o fogo invisível que mantém viva a identidade de um povo. Luiza Berger von Ende é mestra e bacharel em Direito pela Universidade Federal de Santa Maria (UFSM), 1ª Prenda da 13ª Região Tradicionalista (MTG/RS) e membro do Conselho Diretor do Departamento de Tradições Gaúchas Noel Guarany, Programa de Extensão da UFSM e entidade tradicionalista estudantil. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Preservar o fogo, não adorar as cinzas. | Luiza Berger | TEDxUFSM

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What would happen if every person started their day asking, "How can I make a difference today?" In this empowering talk, Marizú Weller Rios, a second-year student at the University of Miami and the founder of Service Central Guatemala challenges the traditional definitions of success and leadership. Drawing from her experiences in her country of origin, she illustrates how the "servant leader mindset" moves us beyond performative volunteering and into a life of genuine impact. She invites the audience to build a culture of service, proving that whether you are a CEO or a student, true leadership is measured by how you lift up those around you.
 Marizú Weller Rios is a passionate and purpose-driven second-year student at the University of Miami, originally from Guatemala City, Guatemala.

title: Building a culture of service | Marizú Weller Rios | TEDxUMiami

description:
This talk unpacks the 4Ps of success—Passion, Plan, Perseverance, and Participate—and how they shape meaningful personal and professional journeys. Drawing from real-life transitions, academic struggles, repeated failures, and eventual breakthroughs, the speaker explains how dreams evolve into goals and goals into purposeful plans. The session highlights the power of consistency, resilience, and collaboration, reminding us that success is not an overnight event but a process built through belief, effort, and active engagement with opportunities and people. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Bu konuşmada Polifish’in kurucusu Tayfun Denizer, girişimcilik yolculuğunda karşılaşılan belirsizlikleri, risk alma cesaretini ve sıfırdan bir marka inşa etmenin görünmeyen taraflarını ele alıyor. Deneyimlerinden yola çıkarak; fikirden ürüne, hayalden gerçeğe giden sürecin arkasındaki zihinsel dayanıklılığı ve stratejik bakış açısını paylaşıyor.
Teknoloji, yenilik ve sürdürülebilir büyüme odağında şekillenen bu konuşma; girişimci olmak isteyenler, kendi yolunu çizmek isteyen gençler ve değişimi başlatma cesareti arayan herkes için ilham verici bir perspektif sunuyor.
 Tayfun Denizer, Karadeniz bölgesinden dünyanın bir çok yerine deniz ürünleri tedariği yapan Polifis şirketinin kurucusudur. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Sakin Bir Deniz Asla İyi Bir Kaptan Çıkarmaz | Tayfun Denizer | TEDxTrabzon University
